blocks.text: Osmoregulation refers to the process by which an organism maintains a stable internal equilibrium of water and dissolved substances, irrespective of the surrounding environmental conditions. Many marine organisms undergo osmosis without the requirement for regulatory systems since their cells have the same osmotic pressure as that of the sea. However, some organisms must actively acquire, retain, or eliminate water or salts in order to regulate their internal water and mineral balance.
